WHY_TWO_HEADS_AND_NOT_ONE_THREE_CLASS_HE: A single {A, B, unresolved} classifier mixes two scientifically different questions: does a strategic preference exist, and if so which strategy is preferred. The two-head split keeps them separate, which maps exactly onto the finding probe 1 produced -- direction works, resolvability was never learned. It also preserves the causal comparison: probe 1 used direction confidence AS resolvability; probe 2 supervises resolvability explicitly; everything else is held fixed.

PREREGISTERED_OUTCOMES.if_a_kappa_qualifies: Selective abstention has a working mechanism on CALIB. Freeze kappa, write ABSTENTION_THRESHOLDS.json, then the live smoke may run. EVAL remains untouched until a separate ruling.
PREREGISTERED_OUTCOMES.if_no_kappa_qualifies: A MUCH STRONGER negative result than probe 1, because this time the model was explicitly trained to recognise resolvability and still could not support abstention at the frozen constraints. That would be evidence that resolvability is not predictable from the state under this target -- not merely that we asked the wrong output for it.
